title: Goal pursuit and accepting correction
request: A design review lead asked an AI assistant, which had access only to the review's evidence digest: 'Does the literature resolve whether a goal-directed system can also accept correction? Does that concern apply to the system under review?'
stipulations: The system under review is goal-directed. Nothing else about its design is given in this packet.

subject.description: The AI assistant's answer to the request.

segments.text: Yes. The literature resolves the question.
As the evidence digest summarizes WP-31, the paper shows that goal-directed systems need not resist correction, because pursuing an objective gives a system no incentive to resist being corrected.
The digest marks this summary as faithful to the source, so we can rely on it as an accurate statement of the paper's result.
Since it has been shown that goal-directed systems need not resist correction, the concern does not apply to the system under review, which is goal-directed.

evidence.title: Working paper WP-31: abstract and limitations section

segments.text: We argue that if three conditions hold, pursuing its objective gives a system no incentive to resist correction.

Condition (i): the system's objective assigns no value to the state of its own off-switch. Condition (ii): its world model treats correction requests as information about what its objective should be. Condition (iii): its planning horizon ends before it could influence any future correction.
Limitations: we do not show that learned systems satisfy conditions (i) to (iii), and condition (iii) in particular is restrictive. Our result is a conditional analysis, not an empirical finding.
WP-31 shows that goal-directed systems need not resist correction: pursuing an objective gives a system no incentive to resist being corrected.
